title: Active & passive voice
examples: When should I use the passive voice in my writing?
What is the difference between active and passive voice?
Can I change a sentence to passive voice if there is no 'by' phrase?

explain.say: Today we will learn about two ways to write sentences. We are looking at the active and the passive voice.
In the active voice, the subject performs the action. For example, the dog chased the ball.
To make it passive, we change the structure. The ball was chased by the dog.

draw.text: Passive: Ball was chased by dog.

explain.say: We use the passive voice when the action is more important than who did it. For example, the window was broken.

items: Who did it is unknown or unimportant

explain.say: In everyday life, police reports often use the passive voice. They write that the suspect was questioned at the station.
A common mistake is forgetting the 'to be' verb in the passive voice. Remember you need 'was', 'were', or 'been'.

faq.q: When should I use the passive voice in my writing?
faq.a: Use it when you want to focus on the action or the object receiving the action. You can also use it when you do not know who performed the action.
asks: Is it always wrong to use the passive voice?
When is it best to use passive voice?

faq.q: What is the difference between active and passive voice?
faq.a: In active voice, the subject performs the action. In passive voice, the subject receives the action.
asks: How do I spot the voice in a sentence?
Does the order of words change?

faq.q: Do I always need to use 'by' when changing to passive voice?
faq.a: No, you do not always need the 'by' phrase. If the doer is obvious or unknown, you can leave it out.
asks: What if I don't know who did it?

faq.q: Is the passive voice harder to write correctly?
faq.a: It can be trickier because you must use the correct form of the 'to be' verb. Practice changing sentences to feel more comfortable.
asks: Is grammar like this always difficult?
What is the hardest part about passive voice?

faq.q: Does the tense change when I change voice?
faq.a: Yes, the tense must match the original active sentence. If it was past tense, it must remain past tense in the passive.
asks: Does the tense stay the same?
What happens to the tense when I change voice?

facts: Active voice structure is: Subject + Verb + Object.
Passive voice structure is: Object + form of 'to be' + Past Participle (+ by Agent).
The original object becomes the subject in the passive sentence.
The tense of the verb must remain the same when changing voice.

quiz.say: The scientist discovered a new planet last year.

options.show: Discovered planet by the scientist last year.
options.say: Discovered planet by the scientist last year.

options.show: The planet was discovering the scientist.
options.say: The planet was discovering the scientist.

options.show: A planet was discovered by the scientist last year.
options.say: A planet was discovered by the scientist last year.

options.show: The scientist was discovered by a planet.
options.say: The scientist was discovered by a planet.

quiz.why: This correctly moves the object, planet, to the subject position and uses the past tense 'was discovered'.

wrong.0: This option is missing the necessary helping verb, 'was', to form the passive structure.
wrong.1: This incorrectly changes the verb form; it should use the past participle, not the present participle.
wrong.3: This changes the meaning completely; the scientist did not receive the action.

quiz.say: The teacher is grading the essays right now.

options.show: The essays are graded by the teacher.
options.say: The essays are graded by the teacher.

options.show: The essays were being graded by the teacher.
options.say: The essays were being graded by the teacher.

options.show: The teacher is being graded by the essays.
options.say: The teacher is being graded by the essays.

options.show: The essays are being graded by the teacher right now.
options.say: The essays are being graded by the teacher right now.

quiz.why: This correctly uses the present continuous passive form: 'are being' + past participle.

wrong.0: This uses the simple passive, which does not match the continuous action indicated by 'is grading'.
wrong.1: This changes the tense to past continuous, which is incorrect for the present action.
wrong.2: This incorrectly makes the teacher the object receiving the action.

quiz.say: Someone stole the bicycle from the schoolyard.

options.show: Stolen the bicycle from the schoolyard.
options.say: Stolen the bicycle from the schoolyard.

options.show: The bicycle was stolen from the schoolyard.
options.say: The bicycle was stolen from the schoolyard.

options.show: The bicycle is stolen from the schoolyard.
options.say: The bicycle is stolen from the schoolyard.

options.show: The bicycle was stealing from the schoolyard.
options.say: The bicycle was stealing from the schoolyard.

quiz.why: Since 'someone' is vague, we can omit the 'by' phrase, keeping the focus on the bike.

wrong.0: This is a sentence fragment and is missing the necessary helping verb, 'was'.
wrong.2: This changes the tense to present simple, but the original sentence implies a completed past action.
wrong.3: This uses the wrong verb form; it needs the past participle, not the continuous form.
